[list-style:none] min-w-0 shrink"><a class="vp-raw transition-colors hover:text-(--Labels-Primary) whitespace-nowrap" href="/en/blog/"><span class="block overflow-hidden min-w-0 whitespace-nowrap shrink text-ellipsis">Research</span></a></li></ol></nav></div><section class="pb-20 w-full"><div class="max-w-none markdown"><h1 node="[object Object]">Introducing PerceptionBench</h1>
<p><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Evaluating Atomic Visual Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models</strong></p>
<p><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Authors</strong> Kimi Team</p>
<hr class="mt-[7px] mb-4 border-t-[0.5px] border-(--Separators-S1)"/>
<h2 node="[object Object]">Overview</h2>
<p>We are releasing <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">PerceptionBench</strong>, a benchmark that isolates visual perception and evaluates it as a set of atomic capabilities—<strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">discovered from how today&#x27;s models fail, not defined in advance.</strong> From frontier-model failures across 42 benchmarks, we derive 10 atomic perceptual capabilities and construct 3,000 verified questions, each isolating a single capability and answerable by looking, with no reasoning or external knowledge required.</p>
<p>Across sixteen frontier MLLMs, no model reaches 60% accuracy, and perception-related hallucination is the weakest capability on average. Models with nearly identical overall scores can diverge sharply in what they actually perceive. PerceptionBench is built to expose exactly where perception breaks, and to drive progress toward multimodal AI that sees faithfully and consistently.</p>
<div class="ImageGrid-module__EsMeTG__imageGridContainer" style="max-width:1080px;margin:0 auto"><div class="ImageGrid-module__EsMeTG__imageGrid" style="gap:16px"><img src="https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-07-24/1d9hj9od3v89kken0j8dg?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1" alt="PerceptionBench versus existing evaluation: an existing benchmark item couples perception with knowledge and reasoning in a single question, while PerceptionBench evaluates ten atomic perceptual categories with one isolating question each" loading="lazy" class="ImageGrid-module__EsMeTG__gridImage" style="flex:1;max-width:100%"/></div></div>
<h2 node="[object Object]">The Dataset</h2>
<p>Guided by the induced taxonomy, we select the most informative failures from the source benchmarks, decompose them into atomic sub-questions, and author additional questions on supplemented images. The retained and constructed samples together form an in-house pool of <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">17,000+</strong> verified questions. The released benchmark subsamples <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">3,000</strong> verified questions from the constructed portion—<strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">60% decomposed</strong> from attributed model failures and <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">40% newly authored</strong>—with category-level balancing and difficulty stratification to isolate atomic perceptual capabilities from confounding factors. The released benchmark distinguishes itself through three core design principles:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Failure-Driven Taxonomy:</strong> Every category is discovered from real model failures, attributed to the earliest erroneous step across 42 existing benchmarks.</li>
<li><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Ten Atomic Perceptual Categories:</strong> Visual Relation, Counting, Attribute, Depth &amp; 3D, Localization, Comparison, Fine-grained Recognition, Context Integration, OCR, and Hallucination.</li>
<li><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Perception, Not Reasoning or Knowledge:</strong> Samples are curated, decomposed, and difficulty-balanced so that difficulty stems from perception rather than reasoning or external knowledge.</li>
</ul>
<div class="ImageGrid-module__EsMeTG__imageGridContainer" style="max-width:880px;margin:0 auto"><div class="ImageGrid-module__EsMeTG__imageGrid" style="gap:16px"><img src="https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/2/2026-07-23/1d9h01rl3v89kkemvehg0?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1" alt="Qualitative examples: four source-benchmark items whose original questions require multi-step solutions are decomposed into atomic perception-only sub-questions, shown with ground truth and the answers of Kimi K3, GPT-5.6-Sol, Claude-Fable-5, and Gemini-3.1-Pro" loading="lazy" class="ImageGrid-module__EsMeTG__gridImage" style="flex:1;max-width:100%"/></div></div>

<p>Each source benchmark captures a narrow slice of perception errors, and these slices overlap only weakly (mean pairwise weighted Jaccard 0.20). No single benchmark—or small group of them—covers perception as a whole, which motivates a capability-centric benchmark that aggregates and rebalances these fragmented views.</p>

<h2 node="[object Object]">Using PerceptionBench to Compare Models</h2>
<!--$?--><div class="my-4 min-h-[160px] animate-pulse rounded-xl bg-(--Fills-F2)"></div><!--/$-->
<div data-blog-hero-width="true"><div class="my-4 animate-pulse rounded-xl bg-(--Fills-F2)" style="min-height:360px"></div></div>
<h2 node="[object Object]">Conclusion</h2>
<p>PerceptionBench is a simple but challenging benchmark for evaluating the atomic visual perception of frontier models. It provides a capability-level standard for measuring and diagnosing the visual perception boundaries of multimodal models. We are open-sourcing the PerceptionBench dataset and evaluation code to help the community address the visual perception gap.</p>
